rationale: Recurring archonic class-noun (lines 4, 26-27): 'principalities of all the archons,' 'all principalities of the kingship.' Etymology unclear; possibly compound on ⲝⲱⲣⲉ 'mighty' or a Manichaean technical term. Translated 'principalities' as best fit. Confidence low.

ⲡⲉⲥ- (her) + ⲓϣ likely = ⲉⲥⲏϣ 'blow, lash, stripe.' Used at the opening of the section describing the punitive exhibition of the bound archons. Antecedent of 'her' uncertain — possibly Hyle/Matter. Confidence low.
Lycopolitan variant of ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise.' Per terminology guide must preserve vertical/exposing semantics. Used here of the punitive raising-up/exposing of the bound archons in shame.
Lyc. verb in ⲛⲉⲧⲁⲩⲕⲁⲧϩⲟⲩ 'those whom they bound.' Possibly = ⲕⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'gather, bind' or ⲕⲱⲧϣ̄ 'turn.' Sequence with ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩⲥ̄ and ⲙⲟⲩⲣ̄ confirms binding sense.
Compound abstract: ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲝⲁⲓ- ('love/boast') + ⲙ̄ⲗⲁⲍ ('strife'). Listed among the archonic vices alongside concupiscence and lust. Cf. accumulated ⲙ̄ⲗⲁϩ 'strife.'
Likely abstract from ⲁϣⲁⲓ 'be many' = 'multitude.' Used at line 29 'multitude of property.' Confidence moderate.
ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('likeness,' per terminology guide) + ⲛⲥⲁⲓ̈ⲉ ('of beauty,' = ⲛⲉⲥⲱ 'beautiful'). The feminine beauty-image bound up with the desire-of-women among the archonic constitutive vices.
Lyc. plural of ⲧⲟⲟⲩ 'mountain.' In line 16 'the mountains which are below' — cosmological pair-partner with 'the heavens' (line 14). The earth's mountains cannot bear the archons either.
